newsitem.title: POLAND: PRESIDENT APPOINTS AIDE BELKA NEW POLISH FINMIN.
newsitem.headline: PRESIDENT APPOINTS AIDE BELKA NEW POLISH FINMIN.

text.p: Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski at a ceremony on Tuesday appointed his economic adviser Marek Belka as new finance minister after accepting the resignation of Grzegorz Kolodko.
Kwasniewski at a ceremony at the presidential palace praised Kolodko for his three years in office after confirming Belka in the position.
"I want to thank Mr Grzegorz Kolodko, who (since the start of the reforms) had filled the most difficult post in the government and his 1112 days in office was our joint success," Kwasniewski said.

Belka, a non-party economist, who has been advising on Kwasniewski on economic policy since his inauguration in late 1995, told Reuters earlier on Tuesday he wanted to continue the government's policy of macroeconomic consolidation, fiscal restraint and fight with inflation.
He said however he wanted to play a more active role in pushing through key structural reforms such as the overhaul of the country's inefficient social security system.
